quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does making eye contact with other drivers mean?

options.text: It is the best way to know that they see you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not guarantee they will yield to you when they should.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee they will yield to you when they should.
questions.explanation: Never assume a driver will yield just because they make eye contact with you. Drivers often look directly at a rider but do not notice they are there.

questions.question: What should you NOT check on your tires?

options.text: Air pressure.
Tread.
General wear.
Flexibility.

questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear. You do not need to check flexibility.

questions.question: What is the correct way to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You can finish passing in a no-passing zone if you started before the zone began.
You can exceed the speed limit to pass.
Pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: Always stay within the speed limit when passing. You can only pass in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Come to a complete stop.
Speed up to create distance between you and them.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. Change lanes when it is safe to do so. Speeding up will only make things more dangerous.

questions.question: What is another name for shifting to a lower gear?

options.text: Engine braking.
Acceleration.
Upshifting.
Coasting.

questions.explanation: When you shift to a lower gear, it works like using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When should you use extra following distance?

options.text: When roads are slippery.
When it is sunny outside.
When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.explanation: Use extra following distance on wet or icy roads. These conditions make it take longer to stop. A two-second distance is normal in good conditions.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Use the brake on the good tire only. As you slow down, carefully move to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What material are riding gloves usually made of?

options.text: Leather.
Wool.
Non-curved material.
Unsafe materials.

questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to increase your visibility to other drivers?

options.text: Wearing proper clothing
Using your headlight at all times
Using your turn signals
Waving at other drivers

questions.explanation: To be visible, wear bright-colored clothing with reflective material, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals and brake lights properly. Waving at drivers is not an effective safety method.

questions.question: When securing a load, where should you place it?

options.text: As high as possible.
As low as possible.
On a sissy bar.
Only on one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Keep loads low. High loads, like those on a sissy bar, raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and make it unbalanced. Spread loads evenly on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks up, what should you do?

options.text: Keep holding the brake and the skid will stop.
Release the front brake and do not use it again.
Release the front brake, then squeeze it quickly.
Release the front brake right away, then apply it smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake immediately. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake.
Squeeze the front brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using both brakes in normal stops helps you be ready if you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective riding gear?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that cover above the ankle
Hearing protection
Pants made of soft material

questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material, boots that cover and support your ankles, and hearing protection even with a helmet.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding, what will happen?

options.text: The steering will feel heavy.
The steering will feel loose.
The steering will feel the same.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, leave the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: What is true about approved helmets?

options.text: They can limit how far you can see to the sides.
They allow you to see far to the sides as needed.
They are dangerous to wear.
You do not have to wear them if they limit your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They allow you to see far to the sides as needed.
questions.explanation: Some people worry that helmets limit side vision, but this is not true. Approved helmets let you see far to the sides as much as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, how does stopping compare to riding without one?

options.text: Stopping is easier with a sidecar.
Stopping takes longer with a sidecar.
You cannot stop with a sidecar.
Stopping is about the same with or without a sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping takes longer with a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight and requires more braking force. Going downhill makes stopping harder. With a sidecar, slowing and stopping take longer.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Do not worry about them.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up.
Leave the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them ahead of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may just make them tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should you position yourself in a lane?

options.text: Always avoid the left portion of the lane.
Always avoid the right portion of the lane.
Always avoid the center of the lane.
Use whatever position in the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whatever position in the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position you must always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, what should you assume about other drivers?

options.text: Assume they see you, especially if they make eye contact.
Never assume they see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection.
Speed up so they notice you.

questions.explanation: Never assume other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look right at a motorcycle and still do not see it. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and jam the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To brake correctly, squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes together when you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move to the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to put distance between you and them.
Ignore them.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make things more dangerous by encouraging them to follow you faster.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular. They have a white background with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, you should use both brakes:

options.text: Only when the pavement is wet.
Not very often.
Only when riding in the city.
Every time.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the strongest stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit?

options.text: In front of the operator.
Behind the operator.
They do not need to reach the footrests.
They should hold the motorcycle frame.

questions.explanation: A child passenger should always sit right behind the operator. If a child sits in front, they may not balance well and could get in the way of the operator's controls.
